detailsHtml:
Introduction: This guide summarizes what the game is and how the main loop fits together, based on the premise and mechanics as presented in-game and on official store listings. For step-by-step inspection habits, use the Rookie Survival Manual and the inspection order & routing protocol.

Part 1: What You Are Playing

Quarantine Zone: The Last Check is a single-player simulation developed by Brigada Games and published by Devolver Digital for Windows PC (Unreal Engine 5). You command a military evacuation checkpoint after a zombie virus outbreak: screen survivors, run the facility, and try to keep infection out of the safe residential side. The PC version is available on Steam; Devolver also lists PC Game Pass as a purchase option—check your regional store page for availability.

Part 2: The Two Modes of Play

The game deliberately splits your attention:

  • First-person checkpoint work: Survivors enter the examination area one at a time. You compare what you see to information in your handbook, use diagnostic tools (for example thermometers, reflex checks, scanners, and lights), and judge how serious reported symptoms look. This is the part reviewers often compare to Papers, Please-style screening: rules, evidence, and moral pressure at the window.
  • Isometric base management: The same commander oversees the checkpoint’s facilities and logistics—sleeping space, power, defenses, generators, and other upgrades funded by what you earn. You are not only stamping papers; you are keeping the post operational.

Part 3: Your Objectives (Why Shifts Feel Tense)

Public descriptions agree on the central tension:

  • You must supply a government-mandated quota of healthy survivors for evacuation within a limited number of days.
  • At the same time, you must keep the virus from reaching the residential / safe zone—one bad clearance can undermine the whole line.
  • Money from inspections and related tasks pays for maintenance and upgrades. If the base fails (power, defenses, capacity), the inspection minigames get harder to “win” cleanly.

Exact quota numbers and day counts are intentionally left to the game UI so this article stays accurate across patches.

Part 4: The Inspection Decision, in Plain Terms

After tools and observation, you route each person into one of the broad outcomes the game is built around:

  • Clear for the residential / safe side when evidence says they are not a credible outbreak risk.
  • Hold in quarantine when signs are ambiguous—buying time at the cost of space and follow-up.
  • Eliminate when the case meets the fiction’s criteria for an active threat (terminology in-game may vary, but the structure is “remove before they breach the safe population”).

For symptom-level detail and tool pairing, use the symptoms wiki and the all-symptoms guide.

Part 5: Progression — Tools and Virus Escalation

Coverage of the game notes that early shifts start with basic checks and that more advanced equipment (deeper scans, imaging, audio-style checks, etc.) appears as the scenario demands. The virus fiction also pushes you toward research and harder reads over time. Treat each new tool as a new failure mode: learn what it confirms, what it cannot see, and when it wastes seconds on an obvious deny or clear.

Part 6: Nights — Hordes and the Combat Drone

When zombie hordes attack at night, you leave the booth routine and pilot a drone armed for defense. Descriptions in reliable summaries frame this as a tower-defense-style layer: positioning, shooting, and keeping the perimeter from collapsing so your daytime economy still has a base. Practical loadout and wave habits are covered in the combat & base defense guide.

Part 7: How This Site’s Guides Map to the Loop

  • Rookie manual + routing protocol: Turn the loop into a repeatable checklist at the window.
  • Contraband / symptoms / wiki: Reference material when the handbook entry alone is not enough.
  • Laboratory & upgrades: Spending pressure between better tools, capacity, and defense.
  • Campaign & moral choices: When narrative events override “pure” mechanics.

Part 8: Staying Accurate

Balance patches, bug fixes, and QoL updates can change timers, economy tuning, or which micro-tasks appear between demo and retail. If something here disagrees with your build, trust the in-game tutorial text and patch notes first; then cross-check our news section for write-ups after major updates.

Conclusion: Quarantine Zone: The Last Check is a checkpoint triage fantasy glued to a base survival backbone. Learn the loop once—inspect → earn → upgrade → survive the night—then drill the window until routing decisions are fast, evidence-based, and honest about risk.

detailsHtml:
Introduction: The Rookie Survival Manual teaches what to look for. This guide locks down when you do each step so you do not double-work survivors, miss contraband, or approve someone because you rushed the UV pass. Pair it with the symptoms guide when a read is ambiguous.

Part 1: Default Tool Order (Every Survivor)

Run this sequence unless the UI or a raid timer forces a shortcut. The goal is cheap information first, then confirmatory scans, then routing.

  1. 360° look + hands: Gait, face, skin, sweat, visible wounds, nervous clutching. Costs nothing and often decides if you even need the body scanner.
  2. Documents: Name, photo match, stamps, expiry. Flag forgeries before you waste tools on a person you will deny anyway.
  3. Thermometer (forehead): Treat 38°C and above as a hard yellow flag — pair with UV and behavior; do not approve on “maybe fine” temperature alone.
  4. UV light (face, neck, hands): Slow pan. You are hunting for fluorescence, odd fluids, and early-stage vein traces. If UV is clean but temp is high, you are still not done.
  5. Metal detector / pat-down flow: If the detector chirps, resolve external pockets → bag → internal scan before final judgment. For X-ray oddities, see the contraband guide.
  6. Body scanner / deep inspection tools: Only after externals are clear. Use when you suspect internal contraband, implants, or organ-level tells the UV missed.
  7. Specialty tools (stethoscope, reflex, eye exam, etc.): Pull these when the generic pass is inconclusive and the case is high risk (VIP, bleeding “scratch” story, silent carrier vibes).

Part 2: When to Pause (Let the Game Show You More)

  • After a stressful question: Some tells appear in dialogue tone or body language a few seconds later. If you already see one red flag, wait one beat before stamping.
  • “Injured, not bitten” claims: Zoom wounds with the magnifier. Clean cuts vs discolored tissue matter; if unsure, watch for a temperature climb over a short window before you commit to Approve.
  • Metal hits but no bag: Do not liquidate for beeps alone — finish the internal scan path or you eat a penalty for wrong deaths and wrong approvals alike.

Part 3: Routing Cheat Sheet

Use this after your tool pass. If two rows conflict, pick the safer row for your run (infection control vs authority loss is campaign-dependent).

Condition Route Why
Docs valid, all tools green, behavior normal Approve → Living / safe zone Max throughput; preserves beds and food if your day is crowded.
Fever or soft symptoms, no hard infection proof Quarantine cell Buys time; better than an interior outbreak. Re-check next cycle if your shift allows.
Needs science you cannot get at the booth (unknown pathogen read) Lab route Unlocks data and upgrades long term; remember lethal tests are a real trade — see lab & upgrades.
Forged papers, major contraband, armed threat Deny / security protocols Keep the gate closed; escalate to combat rules if they draw (see combat guide).
Clear zombie morphology, aggressive UV, parasites, confirmed turn Liquidation Protect the line; verify no civilians in arc before firing.

Part 4: Split Cases (Contraband + Infection Suspicion)

  1. Resolve contraband first so you know if the person is a smuggler, bomber, or both.
  2. Then rerun infection tools — stress and running raise temp; separating the causes avoids false liquidations.
  3. If still split: Quarantine beats Approve; Lab beats guessing when the narrative allows.

Part 5: End-of-Shift Base Checks (30 Seconds)

Before you skip to the next day: generator fuel above the safe band, turret ammo not zero, walls repaired if you took a wave. Details in the defense guide and wiki.

Conclusion: Treat every survivor with the same ordered pass, then route by worst believable risk. Speed comes from muscle memory, not skipping UV.

detailsHtml:
Quarantine Zone: The Last Check – Laboratory & Upgrades Tier List

In Quarantine Zone: The Last Check, money and resources are just as scarce as hope. Making the wrong investment early on can lead to a base blackout or being overrun by a horde. Should you buy that new rifle, or upgrade your X-Ray scanner?

This guide covers the Laboratory mechanics, strategies for organ harvesting, and a complete Tier List of the best upgrades to prioritize for maximum efficiency.

Part 1: The Laboratory & Organ Harvesting

The Laboratory (unlocked around Day 5) is your primary source of Research Points (RP) and a secondary source of income. It allows you to extract organs from infected individuals. For more information about base management and resource strategies, check our base management guide.

Sell vs. Research: The Golden Rule

You have limited storage space in your freezer. Knowing what to keep is crucial:

  • Common Organs (Livers, Kidneys): SELL. These give very low RP but fetch a good price on the Black Market. Use them to fund your daily fuel and ammo costs.
  • Mutated Organs (Blighted Hearts, Spore Glands): RESEARCH. Never sell these. They are required to unlock high-tier Pathology tech like the "Auto-Scanner." Learn more about identifying symptoms and infections in our complete symptoms guide.

Part 2: Checkpoint Upgrades Tier List

Not all tools are created equal. Below is the priority list for spending your cash.

S-Tier (Must-Have Early)

These upgrades fundamentally change how fast you can process survivors.

  • UV Light (Level 2): The base UV light is too dim. Level 2 reveals "Stage 1" spores instantly, saving you from doing a full body search on every person. Master UV light usage techniques in our rookie survival manual or check the symptoms detection wiki.
  • Auto-Translator: Foreign refugees take 2x longer to process without this. It pays for itself within two days by allowing you to process more people.

A-Tier (Get by Mid-Game)

Vital for keeping up with the increasing difficulty.

  • X-Ray Scanner Speed Boost: Later levels require checking stomachs for contraband. The default speed causes long lines; this upgrade fixes the bottleneck. For tips on dealing with invisible contraband bugs, see our contraband detection guide.
  • Drone Repair Kit: Automates the repair of your defense drones, freeing you up to focus on shooting during night raids. Learn advanced combat and defense strategies in our combat & base defense guide.

C-Tier (Avoid / Late Game Only)

  • Aesthetic Upgrades: Paint jobs or flags do nothing for gameplay.
  • Backup Generator: If you manage your fuel correctly, you will never need this.

Part 3: Research Tree Priorities

Once you have harvested enough mutated organs, where should you spend your Research Points?

Branch Skill Name Why it is Essential
Pathology Rapid Diagnosis #1 Priority. It highlights symptoms automatically after 3 seconds of observation. This is the ultimate quality-of-life upgrade. Essential for mastering symptom detection covered in our all symptoms guide.
Military Turret Ammo Capacity Better than damage upgrades early on. Reloading takes precious time during a swarm; larger magazines save lives. Critical for night defense strategies.
Logistics Fuel Efficiency Reduces the daily cost of running the base, effectively increasing your daily profit margin.

Summary

To succeed in Quarantine Zone, prioritize speed over firepower in the early game. Upgrade your UV Light and Translator first to maximize the number of people you check (and pay) per day. Save the combat upgrades for when the hordes start getting bigger around Day 15. For beginners, start with our rookie survival manual, and for advanced strategies, check out our campaign guide on resource management.

detailsHtml:
Quarantine Zone: The Last Check – Internal Contraband Bug Guide

Dealing with quarantine zone contraband is a core mechanic of the game, but recently, many players have reported a game-breaking issue: Internal contraband does not appear on the X-ray scanner, even when the metal detector is beeping loudly.

If you are frustrated by “Poor” inspection ratings because you can’t find the hidden item, you are not alone. This guide explains how the quarantine zone internal contraband system is supposed to work and how to deal with the current invisible item bug affecting Quarantine Zone: The Last Check.

The Problem: “Contraband Items Do Not Appear”

According to numerous reports on the Steam Community, the latest patch appears to have broken the rendering for internal items. The situation usually looks like this:

  • The Symptom: The metal detector beeps, or the survivor behaves nervously, but they have no luggage.
  • The Expectation: You use the X-Ray machine to scan body layers (Skin, Muscle, Bone) to locate swallowed items.
  • The Bug: The X-Ray screen shows nothing. The item is invisible, but the game still penalizes you for missing it.

Is There a Fix for the Invisible Contraband?

At the moment, this is a confirmed bug that the developers are aware of. Until a hotfix arrives, players have found a few workarounds.

1. The “Blind Tagging” Method

Some players, such as Steam user Tempesta, reported success by tagging invisible objects. Even if the item is not visible:

  1. Slowly move your cursor over the survivor’s stomach or chest area while in X-Ray view.
  2. Watch carefully for the UI prompt (usually “E” to Tag) to flicker or light up.
  3. If the prompt appears, press it immediately—even if the screen is empty.

2. The Unfair Unlock Progression Issue

Another issue, reported by user Nurrai, is that the game can spawn survivors with quarantine zone internal contraband before the X-Ray machine is unlocked.

Strategy: During the early game (Days 1–5), if the metal detector triggers on a survivor with no bag and you do not yet have an X-Ray scanner, your only safe option is to Deny Entry. You cannot confiscate the item, and letting them in will damage your reputation.

Standard Quarantine Zone Contraband Guide (When It Works)

Once the bug is patched, this is how contraband detection in Quarantine Zone: The Last Check is intended to function.

External Luggage

  • Backpacks & Suitcases: Always click and drag clothing aside. Contraband is often hidden in the deepest layer.
  • Weapon Permits: Finding a gun is not automatically a crime. Always check for a valid weapon permit before confiscating it.

Internal (Body) Smuggling

  • Metal Detector: Your primary warning system. If it beeps and the survivor has no bag, the contraband is internal.
  • X-Ray Layers: Cycle through layers carefully. Most items (knives, vials) are hidden in the Torso or Legs.

Summary

If you are currently struggling with quarantine zone internal contraband, it is very likely not your fault. The invisible item bug affects most players on the latest patch. Until it is fixed, use the “Blind Tagging” workaround or deny entry to suspicious travelers.

Check back here for future patch note updates.

detailsHtml:
Quarantine Zone: The Last Check – All Symptoms Guide

Quarantine Zone: The Last Check takes a different approach to the zombie genre. Instead of mowing down hordes with a machine gun, your job is to act as the gatekeeper. You must inspect every survivor entering the camp and determine whether they are hiding the virus. For a comprehensive database of all symptoms with detection tools, check our complete symptoms wiki.

To survive, you need to memorize Quarantine Zone: The Last Check all symptoms. Some signs are deadly, while others are harmless traps designed to make you fail. This guide covers everything you need to make the correct decision. For a quick reference table of all symptoms organized by threat level, visit our symptoms detection wiki.

The 3 Categories of Symptoms

Not every ugly mark means infection. All symptoms in the game fall into three categories: Safe (Let In), Suspicious (Quarantine), and Infected (Deny or Kill). For a detailed breakdown of all symptoms with their detection tools, see our symptoms wiki page.

1. “Safe” Symptoms (Do Not Reject)

Many players lose reputation by rejecting survivors who simply look rough. The following visual traits are normal and safe. Learn proper inspection techniques in our rookie survival manual.

  • Yellow Eyes: Unlike many zombie games, yellow eyes are safe here. Do not confuse them with red eyes.
  • Freckles: Natural skin features. Completely safe.
  • Bruises: Blue or purple bruises caused by harsh living conditions. Safe to ignore.

2. “Possibly Infected” Symptoms (Use Quarantine)

These symptoms are uncertain. The survivor may recover or may turn later. Do not let them into the main camp. Send them to the Quarantine Area. For a complete list of quarantine symptoms with detection tools, check our symptoms wiki.

  • Conjunctivitis: Pink or irritated eyes.
  • Skin Cuts: Open wounds that are not bite marks.
  • Fever (Medium): Temperature between 37°C and 41°C.
  • Elevated Pulse: Heart rate between 120 and 180 BPM.
  • Hyper Reflex: Abnormally strong reflex test reaction.

3. “Confirmed Infected” Symptoms (Deny or Kill)

These signs indicate a 100% confirmed infection. There is no cure. See all infection symptoms with their detection methods in our complete symptoms database.

  • Necrosis: Black, dead, or rotting tissue.
  • Bite Mark: The classic zombie bite.
  • Red Eyes: The most reliable infection indicator.
  • Extreme Fever: Temperature above 41°C.
  • Extreme Pulse: Heart rate above 180 BPM.
  • Cross Reflex: A specific abnormal reflex test pattern.

Behavioral Symptoms (Audio Cues)

You do not always need to rely on visuals. Listen carefully while checking documents. The following behaviors are strong warning signs. If detected, send the survivor to Quarantine. Master inspection and interrogation techniques in our survival guide.

  • Sneezing: Often linked to a hidden fever.
  • Hiccups: Frequently associated with heart rate spikes.
  • Coughing: General sickness indicator.
  • Sick Breath: Green fumes or audible cues indicating illness.

Summary Cheat Sheet

Use this quick-reference table for Quarantine Zone: The Last Check all symptoms:

Symptom Status
Yellow EyesSafe (Let In)
FrecklesSafe (Let In)
BruisesSafe (Let In)
ConjunctivitisCheck / Quarantine
Skin CutsCheck / Quarantine
Temperature 37°C – 41°CCheck / Quarantine
Pulse 120 – 180 BPMCheck / Quarantine
Hyper ReflexCheck / Quarantine
NecrosisINFECTED
Bite MarkINFECTED
Red EyesINFECTED
Temperature > 41°CINFECTED
Pulse > 180 BPMINFECTED
Cross ReflexINFECTED

Mastering this list is the only reliable way to keep your infection rate at 0% and your reputation high. Good luck, inspector! For a comprehensive reference table of all symptoms organized by detection tool and threat level, visit our symptoms wiki page.

detailsHtml:
Introduction: In Quarantine Zone, you are not just a bureaucrat with a stamp; you are the gatekeeper of the last line of defense. Every oversight or act of excessive force has severe consequences. This guide will teach you how to survive. For comprehensive information about inspection tools and their usage, check out our complete wiki.

Part 1: The Inspection Process — Observe Like a Hawk

Top inspectors know the rule: "Observe first, test second."

1. Visual Observation (Costs No Resources)

  • Gait & Posture: Watch for limping, twitching, or constant clutching of the stomach/head.
  • Facial Features: Dilated pupils, bloodshot eyes, or vacant stares are strong indicators.
  • Skin: Look for abnormal paleness, black veins, or rashes.
  • Sweat: Excessive sweating usually indicates fever or nervousness.

2. Efficient Tool Usage

  • Thermometer: Aim at forehead. Anything above 38°C is a Red Flag.
  • UV Light (The MVP): Scan face and neck. Look for glowing spots, hidden fluids, or veins.
  • Body Scanner: Check for internal foreign objects (bombs) or organ mutations.

For detailed information about all inspection tools and their advanced usage techniques, visit our wiki section on inspection tools.

Part 2: The Art of Decision Making

  • Green (Approve): All metrics normal, documents match.
  • Yellow (Quarantine): High temp but no other symptoms? When in doubt, quarantine. Better than an outbreak inside.
  • Red (Liquidate): Obvious zombification features, strong positive UV, or parasites. Caution: Ensure no innocents are in the line of fire.

Part 3: Base Management — Logistics Save Lives

Effective resource management is crucial for survival. Learn more about managing your base resources efficiently by checking our resource management guide in the wiki.

  1. Fuel is Life: Always keep the generator fuel above the safety line. No Power = No Lights + No Turrets. Refuel manually in the morning.
  2. Ammo Management: Do not spray and pray. Use pistols for single targets; save heavy ordnance for hordes.
  3. Upgrade Priority: Start with Power Capacity and Tool Efficiency. Later, get Wall Defense.

Part 4: Dealing with Emergencies

  • Raiders: If someone draws a gun, hit the alarm and fire back immediately.
  • Bribes: Reject them. People bribing usually hide infection or heavy contraband.
  • Night Shift: Visibility is terrible. Process the queue before sunset to reduce risk.

Conclusion: In Quarantine Zone, you need to be cold. Trust your gut, Inspector. Good luck.

detailsHtml:
Introduction: While checking paperwork is your day job, staying alive is your night job. As the sun sets, the infected become more aggressive, and raiders see your outpost as a loot box. This guide focuses on the FPS and Tower Defense mechanics to keep your checkpoint standing. For more survival strategies, visit our guides section.

Part 1: The Arsenal — Weapons & Defenses

Your stamp won't stop a horde. Understanding your hardware is the first step to survival.

1. Personal Firearms

  • Service Pistol: Your primary tool for "Liquidation" and minor breaches. Ammo is relatively cheap. Always aim for the head; body shots on infected are a waste of resources.
  • Rifles & Heavy Weapons: Save these for Raiders or Mutated Infected. Do not waste high-caliber rounds on a lone walker.
  • Reload Discipline: Never start an inspection or a night wave with a half-empty magazine.

2. Automated Defenses

  • Sentry Turrets: These are the backbone of your defense. They have perfect aim but consume ammo rapidly. Tip: Check turret ammo levels after every single wave.
  • Combat Drones: Use these to scout outside the perimeter or flank enemies hiding behind cover. They are expensive to replace, so recall them before they take too much damage.

Part 2: Threat Matrix — Know Your Enemy

Different threats require different tactical responses.

  • Walkers (Standard Infected): Slow and predictable. Use the pistol or let turrets handle them if ammo permits. Danger level: Low.
  • Runners (Fresh Infected): Fast and erratic. They will rush the gate immediately. Prioritize them over walkers. Danger level: Medium.
  • Raiders (Humans): The most dangerous threat. They use cover, shoot back, and flank. Tactics: Do not stand still in the window. Use the booth's walls for cover and wait for them to reload or move.
  • Mutants/Tanks: Heavily armored infected. They can destroy your walls in seconds. Focus all fire (Turrets + Player) on them immediately.

Part 3: Fortification Strategy

Strategic base upgrades are essential for survival. Learn about the complete upgrade system in our base upgrade guide.

  1. Lighting is Key: You cannot shoot what you cannot see. Upgrade your Floodlights early. Shadows are where runners hide.
  2. Wall Integrity: Repair your walls every morning. A weakened wall will crumble instantly under a horde attack, letting the infection into the safe zone.
  3. Kill Zones: Position your turrets to create overlapping fields of fire at the main gate. Don't spread them too thin.

Part 4: Crisis Management

  • The Breach: If the outer gate falls, do not die trying to save it. Retreat to the inner checkpoint door and hold the choke point.
  • Friendly Fire: Be careful when using explosives or heavy fire near civilians or infrastructure. Damaging your own generator during a fight is a rookie mistake.
  • Economy of War: Sometimes, it is better to buy ammo than food. You can survive a day of hunger; you cannot survive a night without bullets.

Conclusion: A good inspector is meticulous, but a survivor is lethal. Keep your gun clean, your turrets loaded, and your eyes open.

detailsHtml:
Introduction: In the Campaign Mode, the infected are not your only problem. You are stuck between a demanding Command Center, desperate refugees, and opportunistic insurgents. Your choices at the window don't just affect your salary—they determine if your base rebels, starves, or survives the final wave. This guide covers the narrative threats and special encounters. Stay updated with the latest game news for updates on campaign features.

Part 1: The "Gray Area" Cases (Distinguishing Wounds)

One of the most common narrative traps in the game is the "Injured vs. Infected" dilemma. You will frequently encounter survivors covered in blood or bandages.

1. The "Scratch" Defense

  • Scenario: A survivor has a visible wound but claims it is from a fall or a knife fight, not a zombie.
  • Protocol: Do not trust their dialogue. Use the Magnifying Glass on the wound.
  • Visual Clue: A clean cut or bruise is usually safe. A wound with dark discoloration or puss edges is a bite. If you are unsure, wait. Infected wounds usually trigger a temperature spike within 10 seconds.

2. The Silent Carrier

  • Scenario: They look healthy, act healthy, and plead for entry to see their family inside.
  • The Check: Check their eyes. Even if the skin is clean, the game often hints at infection through erratic pupil movement or a "Dazed" status in their behavior description.
  • Moral Choice: If you reject them, they might beg. If you shoot them, you lose Authority. The safest bet is often the "Quarantine" option if available, or a hard "Deny".

Part 2: Faction Encounters & VIPs

Not everyone is a refugee. You will deal with specific character archetypes that affect your base's story.

1. The Deserters (Military)

  • Clue: They wear torn uniforms and carry military-grade weapons (which you can confiscate for your defense).
  • Risk: Documents often list them as "AWOL" (Absent Without Leave).
  • Decision: Letting them in provides you with strong fighters for the night defense, but Command may penalize your funding for harboring criminals.

2. The Smugglers

  • Clue: They often have incorrect weight stats on their papers.
  • Opportunity: If you catch them, they may offer a Bribe (Fuel/Ammo).
  • Strategy: In the early game, Fuel is scarce. It is sometimes strategically necessary to accept a bribe from a clean smuggler to keep your generator running, even if it hurts your reputation.

3. The VIP / Scientist

  • Event: Command will radio you to prioritize a specific NPC.
  • Protocol: They must survive. Even if they have minor irregularities in their papers, you are often forced to let them through. Provide them with an escort (Drone) if possible.

Part 3: Resource-Based Decision Making

Your inspection choices directly impact your Base Management screen. Understanding resource management is crucial - check our resource management wiki for detailed strategies.

1. Confiscation Economy

  • Mechanic: You have the right to confiscate contraband.
  • Priority: Prioritize confiscating Food Cans, Fuel Canisters, and Weapon Parts. Jewelry or cash is useless if you starve.
  • Tip: If a survivor has "Excess Food" marked as contraband, confiscate it immediately. Your camp's hunger meter rises daily.

2. Labor Force

  • Mechanic: Approved survivors join your camp's population.
  • Balance: More people = More guns on the wall, but also = More mouths to feed.
  • Strategy: If you are low on food, tighten your inspection criteria. Reject anyone who looks weak or elderly (cruel, but necessary for game survival). Only accept able-bodied survivors who can man the turrets.

Part 4: The Night Shift Narrative

The game transitions from "Papers, Please" to a shooter at night. Your day choices dictate the night's difficulty.

  • The Revenge Raid: If you executed a member of the Insurgent Faction during the day (even if they were infected), their allies might launch a retaliatory attack at night. Be prepared for human enemies with guns, not just zombies.
  • The Breach: If you let a "Silent Carrier" in during the day, you won't face a horde outside—you will face an outbreak inside your barracks. This is the worst-case scenario. Always double-check UV scans on suspicious "healthy" people.

Conclusion: In Quarantine Zone, you are writing the story of your camp's demise or survival. Every stamp is a choice between resources, reputation, and safety. Don't be a hero—be a survivor.

seo.description: Stuck on the "Ask Your Mom" objective in Quarantine Zone? Here is the complete walkthrough to find all 6 graffiti poems, solve the red footprints puzzle, and fix the invisible paint bug.

detailsHtml:
Quarantine Zone: The Last Check has captivated players with its intense management mechanics, but one specific objective is causing widespread confusion: the cryptic instruction to "Ask Your Mom."

If you are wandering the camp aimlessly, you aren't alone. This objective is not about finding a character named "Mom," but is actually a linear scavenger hunt for hidden Quarantine Zone poems (graffiti). This comprehensive guide will help you decipher the clue, solve the red footprints puzzle, locate the mysterious survivor with paint on their clothes, and fix common progression bugs.

How to Start the "Ask Your Mom" Quarantine Zone Quest

To complete the "Ask Your Mom" quest in Quarantine Zone: The Last Check, you need to understand the hidden mechanics:

  1. Sequential Spawning: You cannot find all 6 graffiti locations at once. They trigger one by one. You must find the first Quarantine Zone poem to make the second one appear.
  2. The Red Footprints: Once you interact with a poem, look immediately at the ground. You will see a trail of bloody red footprints leading to the next location.
  3. Flashlight is Mandatory: Many players report getting stuck because the footprints are invisible in the dark. Keep your torch (flashlight) ON at all times during this quest to see the trail.

All 6 Quarantine Zone Poems Locations (Graffiti Walkthrough)

Here is the exact step-by-step sequence to find every piece of graffiti. You must visit them in this specific order to progress:

1. Outside the Sleeping Quarters

Start at your command center (the silver container where your bed is). Walk out of the room and look immediately at the concrete wall straight ahead, just to the right of the gate. This is the starting point of the trail.

2. The Blue Potty (Storage Area)

Follow the red footprints along the path towards the Storage area. Look all the way to the far left side. You will see a blue portable toilet (potty). The second poem is scrawled on the wall right next to it.

3. The Lab White Box

Proceed to the Laboratory area. Walk to the far right side of the room. The graffiti is located on the side of a large white box/machine.

4. Behind the Blue Container

Head back towards your sleeping area (Command Center). Identify your own container (it is silver). Walk around behind your container to find a blue storage container tucked in the back. The fourth poem is painted on the back wall of that blue container.

5. The Green Tower

Make your way to the Liquidation area. Look for the tall green tower structure on the left-hand side. The fifth poem is located up on that tower.

6. Inspection Area Wall

Go to the central area where you perform your daily inspections. Turn around (facing back towards your bed) and walk through the gate. Look at the concrete wall at roughly the "1 o'clock" position. You will see the word "Laboratory" stenciled on the wall—the final graffiti is right below it.

How to Complete "Tag the Unknown Symptoms" (The Paint Puzzle)

After finding all Quarantine Zone poems, your objective may update to "Tag the Unknown Symptoms." This is another vague puzzle that has frustrated many players.

  1. The Target: You are looking for a male survivor with blond hair wearing a blue shirt.
  2. The Visual Cue: His clothes should have red paint (or blood) on them.
  3. Location: He is usually found sitting and reading on a bench near the gate in the Survival Block.
  4. The Trigger: Walk up to him and initiate a conversation. He will mention "teaching someone a lesson" and then walk away towards the tents.

Bug Warning: Some players have reported a visual glitch where the red paint does not render on his clothes, or is hidden by a jacket. If you cannot find the visual cue, talk to every survivor in the area. The dialogue will eventually trigger the quest completion even if the paint texture is missing.

Troubleshooting Common Bugs (X-Ray & Inspection Ratings)

The Day 13 X-Ray Scanner Bug

Many players report that the X-ray scanner stops showing contraband items visually.

The Fix: Even if the screen is blank, pay attention to your UI. The "E" prompt to mark an object will still light up when your cursor hovers over a hidden item. Trust the UI prompt, press 'E', and then talk to the survivor to confiscate the invisible item.

"Poor" Inspection Ratings Spike

Around Day 11, it becomes very difficult to get a "Good" rating. This may be due to eye-based symptoms that are hard to detect before unlocking the Eye Scanner upgrade. Be extra thorough with your visual checks during these days.

Summary

The Ask Your Mom quest in Quarantine Zone The Last Check is a guided trail puzzle disguised as exploration. It is not about searching everywhere, but about paying attention to the footprints the game leaves for you. Follow the trail, keep your torch on, and the quest finishes cleanly without bugs or guesswork.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Is the Ask Your Mom quest bugged?
No. The quest is linear and works correctly when completed in order.

Why am I stuck at 3 out of 6 graffiti?
You missed the next set of bloody footprints or skipped a previous graffiti.

Do I need to use the torch?
Yes. The torch makes the footprints visible and prevents missed steps.

Can I complete the graffiti out of order?
No. Only the next graffiti in the sequence will count.

This guide is part of the larger Quarantine Zone The Last Check guides collection.
